title: The Sum of the Left Leaves

concept.title: Tell the child whether it is a left child
body: A **left leaf** is a leaf that is the **left** child of its parent. The root is never a left leaf (it has no parent). When a function looks at a node, it does not know whether the node is a left or right child, unless the **caller tells it**. The simplest way is to check at the parent: when the left child is a leaf, add its value; otherwise recurse into it.
Another way is a flag argument: `walk(node, is_left)`. In both versions the decision uses the **position** of the node, which is a fact about the parent-child link and not about the node alone.

statement: Print the sum of the values of all left leaves of a binary tree: leaves (nodes without children) that are the left child of their parent.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: Print the sum (0 if there is no left leaf).
constraints: The height of a tree is at most 800.
hints: A left leaf is recognised from its parent: the left child exists and has no children.
If the left child is not a leaf, search inside it.
Always search the right subtree as well.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))
